subject.title: fix: copilot token cache ignores profile rotation on rate limit

question: Should the refreshed Copilot token-cache fix persist a truncated hash of the GitHub token, or should it pass and store a non-secret profile/cache identity instead?
rationale: The bug fix is necessary, but the current PR stores a stable credential-derived fingerprint in the credentials cache; choosing that discriminator versus a non-secret profile identity is a security/compatibility boundary decision.

options.title: Use a non-secret cache identity
options.body: Refresh or replace the PR by passing a selected profile/cache identity into the provider-auth helper and storing that instead of a PAT-derived hash when feasible.

options.title: Accept the PAT fingerprint
options.body: Port the current fingerprint approach to provider-auth and document why a 64-bit SHA-256 prefix under the credentials directory is acceptable for this cache discriminator.

options.title: Close and replace the branch
options.body: Close this dirty stale branch after opening or choosing a same-repository replacement that carries the useful fix forward.

recommendation.title: Use a non-secret cache identity
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the PR by passing a selected profile/cache identity into the provider-auth helper and storing that instead of a PAT-derived hash when feasible.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is tied to provider-helper surface alignment and the Copilot provider helper history, making it the best available owner for the cache-boundary choice.
